answer: Each morning a watcher climbs the tower and logs every sighting before noon, and the tower's log guides the caravans that set out that day. A jade sighting invented from the ground fails the log: at the nebula of the tower the watcher must have seen what the log claims, and an invented sighting sends a caravan toward a mirage. Faking the log means posting watchers for a season, logging 200 mornings and paying 7,100, while the wander entry in the tower log is read by the caravan master daily, so a sighting that was never made is crossed out.
